Indexes to top out soon but we see the Nikkei breaking above 70,000 by year-end
CITI'S TAKE

Japanese equities have performed solidly over the past month, despite short-term corrections. Supporting factors have included: 1) hopes for a US-Iran ceasefire agreement and a peak in crude oil prices, 2) the continuation of the global AI and semiconductor boom, and 3) initial company guidance shown in earnings announcements remaining at normal levels of conservatism. Given that not only the Nikkei 225, driven by the tech boom, but also TOPIX recently hit YTD highs, and that earnings revision deterioration is expected in the immediate future, Japanese equities may peak for a while in the short term. However, we conclude that upside potential toward year-end remains significant and that there is no need to change our bullish fundamental view on Japanese equities.

FY26 company plans demonstrate earnings resilience — Japanese companies' FY26 earnings plans as revealed in full-year results suggest firms are anticipating +4.2% YoY revenue growth and +7.6% NP growth (TOPIX basis). We view this as strong guidance given uncertainties around Middle East conditions and widespread cost increases. While profit plan misses may lead to deterioration in earnings forecast revisions in the short term, creating a headwind for stock prices, any deterioration in forecast revisions is likely to be modest given that company plans show normal levels of conservatism. Meanwhile, if earnings beats in high-tech sectors/stocks and margin improvements from pricing pass-throughs support overall earnings, actual corporate earnings are likely to exceed company plans and consensus estimates, with earnings revisions turning upward again.

Japanese equity valuations still have room to rise — We believe margin improvements in an inflationary environment will push up Japanese equity valuations via higher RoE. While TOPIX's 12-month forward PER currently stands at 16.8x, near the upper end of its range over the past decade-plus, we see room for further PER expansion as the average RoE sets its sights on the 11%-12% range. Additionally, 1) globally accommodative financial conditions are keeping global liquidity ample, 2) the Japanese equity market is transforming into an investable market for investors as companies with low RoE that are below the cost of capital fall in number, and 3) Japanese equities still appear relatively undervalued based on yield spreads, which should encourage fund flows from overseas into Japanese equities and support valuations. Based on the above, we set our TOPIX target at 4,500 by applying a PER of 17.5x to FY27 forecast EPS (¥258.4).

"Bad rate rises" unlikely to occur in Japan — From mid to late May, stocks with high valuations, centered on tech, sold off as Japanese long-term rates rose significantly, leading to a short-term correction in Japanese equities overall. However, these moves ended quickly and did not lead to a sustained correction in Japanese equities. We believe "bad rate rises" are unlikely to occur in the Japanese equity market as 1) value stock weightings are high, 2) the economy originally had deflationary tendencies, and 3) the BoJ has an easing bias. However, real rates have been gradually rising recently. If concerns about fiscal deterioration strengthen further and long-term rates rise led by real rates, approaching or exceeding potential growth rates, this could turn into a "bad rate rise."

Continuation of a momentum market is our base case — Under conditions where crude oil prices remain firm and inflationary pressures persist to some degree, we expect mild stagflation, with relatively high inflation coexisting with economic stagnation, to continue. In this environment, our base case is that stocks with independent growth factors not dependent on macroeconomic cycles (“theme” stocks, restructuring stocks, or inflation beneficiaries) will continue to outperform. While buying is currently concentrated in tech among momentum names, if uncertainties around Middle East conditions fall away going forward, buying is likely to spread to lagging momentum stocks (construction, real estate, financials, defense-related, energy). Additionally, while not a momentum sector, automobiles, which have continued to underperform due to bottleneck concerns, appear to have real room for short-term rebounds.
Japanese stocks: firm despite adjustments

Over the last month, Japanese stocks have been resilient, maintaining a firm trend despite some market adjustments. This stability has been supported by several key factors: 1) anticipation of a ceasefire in the Middle East, coupled with a peak in crude oil prices; 2) the ongoing global boom in AI and semiconductors continues to support strong momentum; and 3) the market has taken the generally conservative initial FY3/27 guidance issued by firms alongside full-year FY3/26 results as a positive. Both the Nikkei, heavily influenced by the tech sector, and the broader TOPIX index have recently hit new YTD highs. While a near-term slowdown is possible due to expected guidance cuts, we think the overall potential for growth toward the end of the year remains strong. We see no reason to alter our bullish long-term outlook on Japanese stocks.
FY3/27 company plans demonstrate corporate earnings resilience

The FY3/27 earnings plans presented by Japanese companies at full-year results collectively aim for revenue growth of +4.2% YoY and NP growth of +7.6% on a TOPIX basis. We view these plans as strong given the headwinds, including Middle East uncertainties and widespread cost increases (Figure 1). We interpret the following as demonstrating the resilience of Japanese corporate earnings overall: 1) downside in company estimates versus prior consensus remained at historical average levels despite a highly uncertain macro environment (Figure 2), 2) impressive earnings growth at AI and semiconductor-related stocks, where global strength continues, are pushing up overall earnings performance (Figures 3, 4), and 3) many companies unveiled sales plans that were ahead of prior consensus, confirming their stance on forging ahead with price pass-throughs (Figures 1, 5).

Japanese firms strengthening their ability to smoothly implement price pass-throughs

The company plans presented at full-year results saw a relatively high frequency of sales plan beats and profit plan misses, similar to FY3/23 and FY3/24, when firms were alert to cost increases (Figure 10). We interpret this as firms demonstration of their determination to implement some price pass-throughs while being cautious about whether they can fully pass on higher costs. However, Japanese firms have recently strengthened their ability to more smoothly implement price increases in response to cost increases than in the past, with corporate and consumer price sensitivity to import prices rising (Figure 11). In FY3/23-FY3/24, we saw a pattern of cost increases whereby price hikes led to margin improvement (Figure 12), suggesting guidance that assume implementation of price increases but deterioration in margins is probably too conservative. Given that corporate price pass-throughs have become easier than before and future import price increases are not expected to match 2022 levels (Figure 13), we believe margin deterioration will end more quickly this time. "Bad rate rises" are less likely to materialize in Japan

From mid-to-late May, a significant rise in long-term interest rates prompted a sell-off in high-valuation stocks, especially in the technology sector, causing a brief market-wide adjustment. The adjustment proved temporary, however, and no prolonged market correction ensued. Given higher risk-free rates, long-term rate rises are generally considered valuation compressors for equities. Figure 25 maps out the relationship of long-term rate rises → PER declines, long-term rate declines or sideways moves → PER rises in the case of US equities. Figure 26, meanwhile, shows the strong tendency not just recently but also over the long term in Japanese equities for long-term rates and PER to correlate positively. We see three reasons for the seemingly counterintuitive relationship between Japanese equities and long-term rates: 1) Japanese equities have a lower weighting for growth (high valuation) stocks and a higher weighting for value stocks relative to US equities (Figure 27); 2) while US long-term rate movements are driven primarily by changes in real rates (nominal rates minus inflationary expectations, with longer-term inflationary expectations stable), Japanese long-term rates tend to be strongly influenced by changes in inflationary expectations (Figures 28-31); 3) in Japan there is a bias toward monetary policy easing over the long term, so even if real rates rise somewhat they tend to remain at accommodative levels below potential growth (Figures 32, 33).

However, swings in consensus forecasts have diminished since an IR event in November 2025, where the CEO disclosed quantitative plans for large-scale expansion in SoC tester production capacity in the medium term. Also, we think consensus forecast upside was augmented by management clarity in April 2026 on effectively bringing forward the two- to three-year road map.Buy25,67535,000

We anticipate firm revenue growth in the food business regardless of economic sentiment. A peak in coffee bean prices is also positive for Ajinomoto's margin outlook. Over the medium term we anticipate topline expansion in the non-foods business (functional materials) as Ajinomoto captures AI investment demand, and in the CDMO business being developed we look for sustained contributions to profit growth via a favorable order environment in all business areas.Buy5,3805,500
Gaming & EntertainmentTokiya Baba9697CapcomThe Capcom growth drivers are cumulative software repeat sales generated by core IP Monster Hunter and Resident Evil. The shares are somewhat soft following May 13 results that contained virtually no surprises and we expect a positive response to new title announcements at upcoming industry events. First up are State of Play on June 2, and Summer Game Fest on June 5. This FY's growth stories include repeat sales growth sparked by movie versions of Resident Evil, Devil May Cry, and Street Fighter as well as rising new title sales. The pieces are coming into place for reaching Capcom's 10% annual profit growth target.Buy3,0694,100
IT ServicesMoriya Koketsu6701NECIT services company share prices have fallen sharply since late-January 2026 based mainly on concerns that AI will bring systems development in-house at clients. However, core systems at the likes of NEC and Fujitsu are comparatively isolated from AI substitution, which implies that NEC can reap the AI benefits of development efficiency and accompanying improvement in profitability. Also, NEC is rich in growth stories outside IT services, with high growth potential in defense, aerospace and subsea cables. We have a Buy rating on the shares, seeing particularly inadequate reflection of the growth potential in aerospace and subsea cables.Buy4,3695,300
Machinery, Plant Engineering & ShipbuildingTakahiro Inoue6113AmadaWe forecast a rapid growth trajectory driven by products for data centers and semiconductor packaging (FY3/27E combined sales weighting of 20%-25%). April 2025 acquisition Via Mechanics (develops, manufactures, and sells drills and laser drilling machines for PCBs and semiconductor packaging) is positioned to benefit from growth in investment in semiconductor packaging accompanying growth in demand for AI semiconductors. We note prospects for a FY3/27 earnings beat given conservative guidance.Buy2,9963,500
Pharmaceuticals & Medical EquipmentHidemaru Yamaguchi4519Chugai PharmaceuticalWe highlight prospects for steady growth on the royalties from oral GLP-1 agonist Fondayo, which is licensed to Eli Lilly (approval obtained April 1). Fondayo's initial prescription numbers were strong but the drug's reputation has fallen because it lags competitors. We remain upbeat however, in anticipation of rising numbers (we still assume end sales of ¥6trn, royalties of ¥780bn). We also note Chugai's strong drug discovery capabilities in respect to Emugrobart, a myostatin antibody licensed to Roche. Emugrobart is in a combination study with a GLP-1 antagonist for increasing muscle mass, with prospects for Phase 2 results release in 2026. For the medium term, Chugai has numerous new drugs with blockbuster prospects including mid-size molecule anticancer drugs, and the NXT007 successor to hemophilia treatment Hemlibra.Buy7,66413,500
Real Estate, J-REIT, HousingMasashi Miki, CFA8802Mitsubishi EstateWe like the firm's orientation toward RoE improvement and accelerated profit growth over the longer run. In addition to stable NOI growth from a blue-chip portfolio centered on the Marunouchi and Otemachi areas of central Tokyo, we expect continued improvement in capital efficiency and higher profit levels to result from progress in recycling capital both domestically and overseas. Investment in data centers in the US is a driver unique to Mitsubishi Estate. We also see room for further expansion in shareholder returns.Buy3,9265,000
Telecommunication / InternetKeiichi Yoneshima6098Recruit HoldingsKey US unit Indeed is growing revenues on quality enhancement in a shrinking US job ad market. We have a positive take on the results delivered by shifting the business model to quality from volume despite a challenging market environment. US Indeed is sustaining double-digit growth in average revenue per job posting (ARPJ), looking for 18% growth in FY3/27. Earnings growth is backed by proactive AI deployment in raising cost efficiency and growing earnings. The shares were weak until FY3/26 results and we expect them to be marked up on recognition of the AI skills. Recruit guides for continued high growth of 9% in revenues and 25% in OP in FY3/27.Buy10,90011,000

spans.content: Guide to Citi Fundamental Research Investment Ratings:
Citi stock recommendations include an investment rating and an optional risk rating to highlight high risk stocks.
Risk rating takes into account both price volatility and fundamental criteria. Stocks will either have no risk rating or a High risk rating assigned.

Investment Ratings: Citi investment ratings are Buy, Neutral and Sell. Our ratings are a function of analyst expectations of expected total return ("ETR") and risk. ETR is the sum of the forecast price appreciation (or depreciation) plus the dividend yield for a stock within the next 12 months. The target price is based on a 12 month time horizon. The Investment rating definitions are: Buy (1) ETR of 15% or more or 25% or more for High risk stocks; and Sell (3) for negative ETR. Any covered stock not assigned a Buy or a Sell is a Neutral (2). For stocks rated Neutral (2), if an analyst believes that there are insufficient valuation drivers and/or investment catalysts to derive a positive or negative investment view, they may elect with the approval of Citi management not to assign a target price and, thus, not derive an ETR. Citi may suspend its rating and target price and assign "Rating Suspended" status for regulatory and/or internal policy reasons. Citi may also suspend its rating and target price and assign "Under Review" status for other exceptional circumstances (e.g. lack of information critical to the analyst's thesis, trading suspension) affecting the company and/or trading in the company's securities. In both such situations, the rating and target price will show as “—” and “-” respectively in the rating history price chart. Prior to 11 April 2022 Citi assigned "Under Review" status to both situations and prior to 11 Nov 2020 only in exceptional circumstances. As soon as practically possible, the analyst will publish a note re-establishing a rating and investment thesis. Investment ratings are determined by the ranges described above at the time of initiation of coverage, a change in investment and/or risk rating, or a change in target price (subject to limited management discretion). At times, the expected total returns may fall outside of these ranges because of market price movements and/or other short-term volatility or trading patterns. Such interim deviations will be permitted but will become subject to review by Research Management. Your decision to buy or sell a security should be based upon your personal investment objectives and should be made only after evaluating the stock's expected performance and risk.

A Catalyst Watch will be published when Analyst confidence is high that an impact to share price will occur; it will be a STV when confidence level is moderate. A Catalyst Watch or STV Upside/Downside call will automatically expire at the end of the specified 30/90 day period. The Catalyst Watch will also be automatically removed if share price performance (calculated at market close) exceeds 15% against the direction of the call (unless over-ridden by the analyst). The analyst may also remove a Catalyst Watch or STV call prior to the end of the specified period in a published research note. A Catalyst Watch/STV Upside or Downside call may be different from and does not affect a stock's fundamental equity rating, which reflects a longer-term total absolute return expectation. For purposes of FINRA ratings-distribution-disclosure rules, a Catalyst Watch/STV Upside call corresponds to a buy recommendation and a Catalyst Watch/STV Downside call corresponds to a sell recommendation. For purposes of FINRA ratings distribution-disclosure rules, we correspond Catalyst Watch/STV No View to Hold in our ratings distribution table for our Catalyst Watch/STV Upside/Downside rating system. However, we reiterate that we do not consider No View to be a recommendation.
